newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end down in light volume trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end down in light volume trade.

text.p: Manila stocks finished down on Tuesday amidst thin trading, pulled down by selling in blue chips, traders said.
"There's selling on good news. Now that APEC is over, market is correcting. Most blue chips are down," said Teresa Lee, Lippo Securities assistant vice-president.
The main index closed 30.18 points lower, or 0.97 percent, at 3,074.28 points.
Value of shares traded was thin at 2.4 billion pesos. Losers trounced gainers 71 to 48 with 76 unchanged issues.
Irving Ackerman, president of I.Ackerman & Co Inc said that heavy selling marked PNB shares. "I'm very disappointed at the market. Somebody, a foreign broker decided to dump PNB shares."
A Standard & Poor's comment on local banks overexposure to the property sector may have triggered the sell-off in PNB shares, Peregrine Securities (Phils) Inc analyst said.
"Market will likely move sideways for the rest of the week until it finds direction," said Barrientos.
